mainTopic: Trapping from ביברין on יום טוב, the definition of מחוסר צידה, and fish from traps or of doubtful readiness (ספק מוכן)
overview: The amud opens with the end of a משנה: an animal in an enclosure that still needs real trapping (מחוסר צידה) may not be taken on יום טוב, but one that can be grabbed right away may be taken. The גמרא sets a ברייתא against this. The ברייתא forbids trapping animals and birds from ביברין on יום טוב. The גמרא first explains the animal clash as a מחלוקת between רבי יהודה and חכמים. For birds it suggests a roofed vs. unroofed ביבר. It defends that suggestion by saying the 'bird in a house is not caught' rule is only about a צפור דרור. Then it explains the animals the same way, as a small vs. large ביבר, and רב אשי gives three ways to tell them apart. Next, שמואל rules like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, which leads to אביי's famous point that we must understand, not just repeat a ruling. שמואל defines מחוסר צידה as 'bring a trap'. That test is refined using geese, chickens and dovecote doves. A new משנה then says animals from traps set before יום טוב may be taken only if they were caught before יום טוב. The גמרא fills in missing words to fit the story of רבן גמליאל and the fish, and שמואל rules that ספק מוכן is forbidden. A third version of that ruling begins at the end and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The משנה's rule: needs trapping is forbidden, does not need trapping is allowed
steps.stepSummary: The משנה closes with a general rule. If an animal still needs to be caught, taking it is forbidden on יום טוב. If it can be grabbed right away, taking it is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the animal still needs trapping, it is forbidden. If it does not need trapping, it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the end of the משנה. It gives the test for when you may take an animal out of an enclosure on יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key question is whether the animal counts as already caught. If you would still have to chase it, taking it is a new act of צידה, which is forbidden. If you can simply grab it, it is already 'caught', so taking it is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: Still needs trapping. The animal is not yet really caught.
Trapping or hunting, one of the forbidden מלאכות.

steps.whyThisMatters: This 'מחוסר צידה' test is the yardstick the whole סוגיא uses to decide whether an animal is already considered caught.

phrases.english: One whose trapping is still lacking — is forbidden,
phrases.notes: He means an animal you would still have to chase and catch inside the enclosure.

phrases.english: and one whose trapping is not lacking — is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closing line of the משנה, which began earlier on the daf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An animal that still needs trapping may not be taken on יום טוב. One that does not need trapping may be taken.

steps.title: A ברייתא forbids trapping from enclosures, contradicting the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא that says you may not trap animals or birds from ביברין on יום טוב, and may not even feed them. This clashes with the משנה about animals and also about birds.
steps.simpleTranslation: The גמרא raises a contradiction: a ברייתא says you may not trap from animal or bird enclosures on יום טוב, and you may not put food in front of them. So the rulings about animals contradict each other, and the rulings about birds contradict each other!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by setting a ברייתא against our משנה. It points out two separate contradictions, one about animals and one about birds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the משנה allowed taking animals and birds from ביברין, as long as they are not מחוסר צידה. The ברייתא flatly forbids trapping from ביברין of animals and of birds. Because both sources talk about the same two kinds of creatures, the גמרא lists the contradiction twice.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And they contrasted them.' The formula for raising a contradiction between two sources.
Enclosures or preserves where animals or birds are kept.
It is difficult. Introduces a problem.

steps.confusionAlert: There are two separate questions here, animals and birds. The גמרא will answer them one at a time, so do not expect one answer to cover both.

phrases.english: GEMARA: And they raised a contradiction:
Enclosures of animals and of birds —
one may not trap from them on a Festival,
and one may not put food before them.
It is difficult: animal against animal,
phrases.notes: He means the משנה's ruling on animals clashes with the ברייתא's ruling on animals.

phrases.english: it is difficult: birds against birds!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the משנה's permission to trap from ביברין.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that animals and birds may be taken from ביברין on יום טוב.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא forbids trapping from those same ביברין, for both animals and birds.

steps.title: The animal contradiction is solved: two different תנאים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the animal contradiction is easy to solve. The ברייתא follows רבי יהודה and the משנה follows רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: The contradiction about animals is no problem. This source follows רבי יהודה, and that one follows רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the first half of the question, about animals. The word בשלמא signals that the bird question is still waiting.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is no real contradiction because the two sources reflect a מחלוקת. For רבי יהודה, an animal in a ביבר is not yet considered caught, so taking it is forbidden, as the ברייתא says. For רבנן it is already caught, so taking it is allowed, as the משנה says.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Granted.' This part is fine, but another part is still a problem.
This one ... that one. Each source is assigned to a different opinion.

steps.confusionAlert: בשלמא does not mean everything is solved. It means 'this part works', and it hints that the bird part is still a problem.

phrases.english: Granted, animal against animal is not difficult:
this one is Rabbi Yehuda, that one is the Rabbis.
phrases.notes: The ברייתא that forbids follows רבי יהודה. Our משנה that permits follows the Rabbis.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the animal half of the קשיא in step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning the two sources to different תנאים (רבי יהודה vs. רבנן).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both sources seemed to give one rule about animals in ביברין, so they appeared to contradict.
steps.terutzMaskana: They follow different opinions: the ברייתא follows רבי יהודה, the משנה follows רבנן.

steps.title: Proof that רבי יהודה and חכמים disagree about animals in enclosures
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה about trapping on שבת. רבי יהודה makes one liable only for chasing a deer into a house, not into a ביבר. חכמים make one liable even for chasing it into a ביבר.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: רבי יהודה says, one who traps a bird into a closet or a deer into a house is liable. Only into a house is he liable, but into an enclosure he is not. חכמים say: a bird into a closet, and a deer into a garden, a courtyard, or an enclosure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source to prove that רבי יהודה and רבנן really disagree about whether an animal in a ביבר counts as caught.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יהודה, driving a deer into a ביבר is not liable, which means it is not yet caught there. So taking it out later would still be trapping. For חכמים it counts as caught in a ביבר, so taking it out on יום טוב is not new trapping. Notice that both agree a bird counts as caught only in a closet, so this proof does not settle the bird contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: A closet or cabinet, a small closed space.
Liable (on שבת, for doing a מלאכה).

steps.whatToRemember: For animals: רבי יהודה says an animal in a ביבר is not caught (matching the ברייתא), and חכמים say it is caught (matching our משנה). This does not solve the bird contradiction, because on birds both opinions agree. Steps 5-9 deal with the birds.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the יום טוב question depends on the same idea as the שבת liability: at what point does an animal count as caught.

phrases.english: As we learned in a mishna: Rabbi Yehuda says:
One who traps a bird into a closet
or a deer into a house — is liable.
It is into a house that he is liable,
but into enclosures — not.
And the Sages say: a bird — into a closet,
and a deer — into a garden, a courtyard, or enclosures.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for the claim in step 3 that רבי יהודה and רבנן disagree.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יהודה and רבנן disagree about whether an animal in a ביבר counts as caught.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about trapping on שבת: רבי יהודה makes one liable only for chasing a deer into a house, while חכמים include a ביבר.

steps.title: The bird contradiction is still unsolved
steps.stepSummary: The רבי יהודה / רבנן answer works for animals, but the contradiction about birds remains.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the birds-against-birds contradiction is still difficult!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says that the animal problem was solved, but the bird problem is still open. This sets up the search for a new answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 4's משנה about שבת, both רבי יהודה and חכמים agree about birds: a bird is only trapped when chased into a closet, not into a house. So splitting the משנה and the ברייתא between רבי יהודה and רבנן cannot explain why one permits catching birds from a ביבר and the other forbids it.

keyTerms.meaning: birds against birds: the two sources clash about birds
it is difficult, a contradiction remains

phrases.english: But the ruling about birds against the ruling about birds is difficult!
phrases.notes: Since רבי יהודה and the רבנן agree about birds, the earlier answer does not help here.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the answer of step 3 (backed by step 4) to animals only, and reopens the bird half of step 2's contradiction.
steps.kashyaTarget: The contradiction between the משנה and the ברייתא about catching birds from a ביבר on יום טוב
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The תנאים in step 4 do not argue about birds, so the bird contradiction cannot be explained as a מחלוקת.

steps.title: Suggested answer: roofed vs. unroofed enclosure
steps.stepSummary: Someone might suggest that the משנה is talking about a roofed ביבר and the ברייתא about an unroofed one.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say this is also not difficult: this source is talking about a roofed enclosure, and that source is talking about an enclosure that is not roofed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a possible answer for the birds ('if you would say'). It is setting this answer up so it can test it in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that a bird in a roofed ביבר cannot fly away, so it counts as already caught and taking it is allowed (the משנה). In an unroofed ביבר it can fly out, so taking it is real trapping and is forbidden (the ברייתא).

keyTerms.meaning: and if you would say (a suggested answer that the גמרא is about to test)

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי תֵּימָא הָא נָמֵי לָא קַשְׁיָא:
phrases.english: And if you say this is also not difficult:
this one is about a roofed enclosure,
phrases.notes: 'This one' is our משנה, which allows taking the bird.

phrases.english: that one is about an enclosure that is not roofed.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא הָא נָמֵי לָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proposes a factual distinction to solve the bird contradiction raised in step 5.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two sources about birds really contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: Suggested: they describe different enclosures, roofed vs. unroofed. This is tested in the next step.

steps.title: Challenge: a bird in a house is not trapped
steps.stepSummary: A house is like a roofed ביבר, and everyone agrees a bird in a house is not considered caught. So the roofed-enclosure answer fails.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a house is just like a roofed enclosure, and both according to רבי יהודה and according to the רבנן, a bird chased into a closet, yes, it is trapped; into a house, no, it is not!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the roofed-enclosure answer, using the שבת משנה from step 4.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides in the שבת משנה agree that a bird inside a house is not yet trapped, because it can still fly around. A roofed ביבר is no different from a house. So a bird in a roofed ביבר should also not count as caught, and the משנה's permission cannot be about that case.

keyTerms.meaning: but look, isn't it so that (opens a challenge)
is similar to, is treated like
a closet / cabinet: a small closed space

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two places: a מִגְדָּל here is a small closet where the bird is truly stuck, not a big tower. A בַּיִת (house) is big enough for the bird to keep flying away.

phrases.english: But a house, which is like a roofed enclosure,
both according to רבי יהודה and according to the רבנן:
a bird chased into a closet, yes, it is trapped,
phrases.notes: This comes from the same שבת משנה as step 4, which also talks about birds.

phrases.english: into a house, no, it is not!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the roofed/unroofed distinction offered in step 6.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole roofed-enclosure answer for birds
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A roofed ביבר is like a house, and all agree a bird in a house is not trapped. So the משנה cannot be allowing birds from a roofed ביבר.

steps.title: רבה בר רב הונא: that rule is about a צפור דרור
steps.stepSummary: The rule that a bird in a house is not trapped refers only to a צפור דרור, a wild bird that never accepts control.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר רב הונא said: Here we are dealing with a צפור דרור, which does not accept authority.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה בר רב הונא defends the roofed-enclosure answer by narrowing the שבת rule to one special kind of bird.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The שבת משנה says a bird in a house is not trapped only because it speaks about a צפור דרור, which keeps flying freely even indoors. Ordinary birds in a house or a roofed ביבר do count as caught. So the roofed vs. unroofed answer from step 6 works again.

keyTerms.meaning: a 'free bird' (a sparrow-type bird) that cannot be tamed

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the 'house' rule for birds is not about all birds. It is about this one wild kind, so it no longer clashes with the roofed-enclosure answer.

phrases.english: רבה בר רב הונא said:
Here we are dealing with a free bird,
phrases.notes: 'Here' means the שבת משנה that said a bird in a house is not trapped.

phrases.english: which does not accept authority.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא: הָכָא בְּצִפּוֹר דְּרוֹר עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 7's rejection and brings back step 6's roofed/unroofed answer.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case (narrowing which bird the source is talking about)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any bird in a house or a roofed space is not considered trapped.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a צפור דרור stays free indoors. Other birds in a roofed ביבר are caught, so the משנה (roofed) and the ברייתא (unroofed) don't clash.

steps.title: Support from the school of רבי ישמעאל
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא explains that the name דרור means the bird 'dwells' freely in a house just as in a field.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the school of רבי ישמעאל taught: Why is it called a צפור דרור? Because it dwells in a house just as it does in a field.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a teaching that backs up רבה בר רב הונא's description of the צפור דרור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The name דְּרוֹר is linked to דָּרָה, 'dwells'. The bird lives in a house as freely as outdoors, flying from place to place. This proves that being inside a house does not trap it, which is exactly the point רבה בר רב הונא needs.

keyTerms.meaning: the school of רבי ישמעאל taught (a ברייתא)

phrases.english: As the school of רבי ישמעאל taught:
Why is it called a free bird?
Because it dwells in a house as in a field.
phrases.notes: A play on words: דְּרוֹר sounds like דָּרָה, 'dwells'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a source supporting step 8's claim that a צפור דרור does not accept control.
steps.raayaObject: That a צפור דרור is not trapped even inside a house
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא of the school of רבי ישמעאל explaining the name דרור

steps.title: Animals too: small vs. large enclosure
steps.stepSummary: Now that the sources are explained as different situations, the animal contradiction is solved the same way: small ביבר vs. large ביבר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now that you have come to this, the animal-against-animal contradiction is also not difficult: this one is about a small enclosure, and that one is about a large enclosure.
steps.whatsHappening: Using the same kind of thinking, the גמרא gives a new answer for animals that does not need a מחלוקת between תנאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before, the animal contradiction was solved by saying רבי יהודה and רבנן argue (step 3). Now the גמרא says both sources can agree. In a small ביבר the animal is easy to grab, so the משנה allows it. In a large ביבר it can still run away, so catching it is real trapping and the ברייתא forbids it.

keyTerms.meaning: now that you have come to this (approach)
animal against animal: the clash about animals

steps.whatToRemember: Final picture: the משנה and the ברייתא do not argue. Birds: roofed ביבר is allowed, unroofed is forbidden (except a צפור דרור, which is never caught just by being indoors). Animals: small ביבר is allowed, large is forbidden. The test is always the משנה's rule: can it be grabbed right away, or does it still need catching?

phrases.english: Now that you have arrived at this,
phrases.notes: 'This' means explaining the two sources as different situations instead of a מחלוקת.

phrases.english: animal against animal is also not difficult:
this one is about a small enclosure,
that one is about a large enclosure.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַשְׁתָּא דְּאָתֵית לְהָכִי, חַיָּה אַחַיָּה נָמֵי לָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the different-situations approach from steps 6-9 to replace step 3's מחלוקת answer for animals.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases (size of the enclosure)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The animal contradiction must be a מחלוקת between רבי יהודה and רבנן.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both sources agree. A small ביבר is allowed and a large ביבר is forbidden.

steps.title: What counts as a small or large enclosure
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how to define a small ביבר and a large ביבר.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is a small enclosure, and what is a large enclosure?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא just said the animal sources differ because one is a small ביבר and one is a large ביבר. Now it asks how we tell which is which, setting up רב אשי's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer in step 10 depends on a size difference, but 'small' and 'large' are vague. The גמרא wants a clear measure so the rule can actually be used.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? How do we picture it?

phrases.english: What is the case of a small enclosure
and what is the case of a large enclosure?

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵיכִי דָּמֵי בִּיבָר קָטָן הֵיכִי דָּמֵי בִּיבָר גָּדוֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for a definition of the terms used in the answer of step 10.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A practical measure for telling a small ביבר from a large one.

steps.title: First definition: caught in one lunge
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי: if you can run after the animal and grab it in one lunge, it is a small ביבר. Otherwise it is large.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: Any enclosure where a person can run after the animal and reach it in one lunge is a small enclosure. Any other enclosure is a large one.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives his first way to measure: how easy it is to catch the animal by running after it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If one quick lunge is enough, the animal is basically already caught, so taking it is not new trapping. If it takes more effort than that, the animal still needs real catching.

keyTerms.meaning: And the other, meaning anything else

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
Any place where one runs after it
and reaches it in one stoop
phrases.notes: A 'stoop' here means one bend or lunge to grab the animal.

phrases.english: is a small enclosure,
and the other is a large enclosure.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: כׇּל הֵיכָא דְּרָהֵיט אַבָּתְרַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Small means the animal can be caught with one lunge.

steps.title: Second definition: many corners
steps.stepSummary: Another option: if the enclosure has many corners, it is a large ביבר. Otherwise it is small.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or perhaps: any enclosure that has many corners is a large enclosure, and any other is a small one.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי offers a second possible measure, based on the shape of the enclosure instead of its size.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Corners give the animal places to hide and slip away, so catching it takes real effort. That makes it count as a large ביבר even if the space is not big.

phrases.aramaic: אִי נָמֵי: כׇּל הֵיכָא דְּאִיכָּא עוּקְצֵי עוּקְצֵי
phrases.english: Or perhaps: any place where there are many corners
is a large enclosure,
and the other is a small enclosure.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי נָמֵי: כׇּל הֵיכָא דְּאִיכָּא עוּקְצֵי עוּקְצֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second possible answer to step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Many corners make it a large ביבר.

steps.title: Third definition: walls' shadows overlap
steps.stepSummary: A third option: if the shadows of the walls fall on each other, it is a small ביבר. Otherwise it is large.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or perhaps: any enclosure where the shadows of the walls fall on one another is a small enclosure, and any other is a large one.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives a third possible measure, based on how close the walls are to each other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the walls are close enough that their shadows meet, the space is tight and the animal cannot get far. When the walls are farther apart, the space is open and catching the animal takes work.
steps.whatToRemember: There are three possible measures for a small ביבר: one lunge catches the animal, there are no hiding corners, or the walls are so close that their shadows overlap.

phrases.english: Or perhaps: any place
where the shadows of the walls fall on each other
is a small enclosure,
and the other is a large enclosure.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי נָמֵי: כׇּל הֵיכָא דְּנָפְלִי טוּלָּא דְכֻתְלֵי אַהֲדָדֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a third possible answer to step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Overlapping wall shadows make it a small ביבר.

steps.title: The ruling follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבן שמעון בן גמליאל from the משנה, and שמואל rules that the הלכה follows him.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says not all enclosures are the same. רב יוסף said in the name of רב יהודה, who said in the name of שמואל: The הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה and gives a practical ruling on it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says it depends on the enclosure: in some the animal is already counted as caught and in others it is not. שמואל says we follow that approach in practice.

keyTerms.meaning: Not all enclosures are the same
Etc.; the rest of the משנה quote

phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says
not all enclosures are the same, etc.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: Rav Yosef said that Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
The halacha is in accordance with Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר לֹא כָּל הַבֵּיבָרִין שָׁוִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to a new line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל that it depends on the type of enclosure.

steps.title: אביי: does 'הלכה' mean there is a dispute?
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks whether saying 'the הלכה follows him' means the רבנן actually disagree with רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: You said 'the הלכה' follows him. That implies they disagree!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי asks a question about שמואל's ruling: is there really an argument here at all?
steps.deeperAnalysis: We usually only say 'the הלכה follows X' when someone argues with X. אביי is unsure whether רבן שמעון בן גמליאל is arguing with the רבנן or only explaining what they meant.
steps.confusionAlert: אביי is not challenging the ruling itself. He is asking whether there is really a dispute behind it.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
'Halacha' implies that they disagree!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: הֲלָכָה מִכְּלָל דִּפְלִיגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions what the wording of step 15 implies.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the רבנן truly disagree with רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.

steps.title: רב יוסף: what difference does it make?
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers back: either way the הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, so why does it matter?
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: And what difference does it make to you?
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף pushes back on אביי's question and says it has no practical result.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Whether or not there is a dispute, we still act like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. So רב יוסף asks why the question is worth asking.

keyTerms.meaning: What difference does it make to you?

phrases.english: He said to him:
And what difference does it make to you?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges whether the question in step 16 matters.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The practical law is the same either way, so the question seems pointless.

steps.title: אביי: learning is not just reciting a song
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that we must understand what we learn, not just repeat it like a song.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: 'Learn the lesson, and let it be a song'?!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי defends his question. Understanding the sources matters even when the practical result does not change.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי uses a popular saying that mocks someone who just repeats a ruling without understanding it. Learning means knowing why, not only knowing what to do.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a well-known statement that Torah learning has value even with no practical difference in הלכה.

phrases.english: He said to him: Learn the lesson,
and let it be a song?!
phrases.notes: He means: should we just sing back the ruling without understanding it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב יוסף's challenge in step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Understanding the sources is valuable on its own, even without a practical difference.

steps.title: What is an animal still needing to be caught?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's general rule about מחוסר צידה and asks what it means.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: This is the rule: any animal that still needs catching, etc. What is the case of an animal that still needs catching?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the משנה's summary rule and asks for a definition, setting up שמואל's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה forbids taking on יום טוב an animal that is מחוסר צידה, one that still needs to be caught. The גמרא wants to know exactly when an animal counts that way.

phrases.english: This is the rule:
any animal that still needs catching, etc.
What is the case of an animal that still needs catching?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next line of the משנה.

steps.title: Definition: when people would say 'bring a trap'
steps.stepSummary: שמואל: an animal is מחוסר צידה if people would say 'Bring a trap so we can catch it.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said that רב יהודה said that שמואל said: Any animal about which a person would say, 'Bring a trap and we will catch it.'
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל gives a simple real-life test for when an animal still needs catching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If you would need a trap to get the animal, it is not yet caught, and taking it on יום טוב counts as trapping. If you can just take it by hand, it is already considered caught.
steps.whatToRemember: שמואל's basic test: מחוסר צידה means you would need a trap to get the animal. The next steps refine it, because geese and chickens also need a trap yet already count as caught.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: Rav Yosef said that Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
Any animal about which one says: Bring a trap and we will catch it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: An animal that would need a trap to catch is מחוסר צידה.

steps.title: אביי challenges the definition from geese and chickens
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks: people would say 'Bring a trap' about geese and chickens, yet a ברייתא rules that trapping them is פטור.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: But geese and chickens are animals people would say 'Bring a trap so we can catch it' about, and a ברייתא teaches that one who traps geese, chickens or home-raised doves is exempt!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks שמואל's definition of מחוסר צידה by pointing to a case where it seems to give the wrong answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Loose geese and chickens run away, so people do need a trap to catch them. By שמואל's test they should count as not yet trapped. Yet a ברייתא says trapping them is פטור, meaning they already count as caught. So the test seems too broad.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
But aren't geese and chickens
creatures about which people say, 'Bring a trap so we can catch it'?
And it is taught:
One who traps geese and chickens
and home-raised doves is exempt!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the definition of מחוסר צידה given in Step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's test: an animal is מחוסר צידה if people would say 'Bring a trap.'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Geese and chickens pass the 'bring a trap' test, yet a ברייתא treats them as already caught (פטור). So the test cannot be the whole story.

steps.title: First answer: geese and chickens come home at night
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר רב הונא in שמואל's name: geese and chickens come back to their coop every evening, but the other animals do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר רב הונא said in the name of שמואל: These (geese and chickens) come into their coop in the evening, and those do not come into their coop in the evening.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers אביי by pointing to a difference between geese and chickens and the animals in the משנה's case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though geese and chickens run around by day, they return home on their own each night. That makes them count as already in your control. The animals in the משנה's case never come home, so catching them is real trapping.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: Rabba bar Rav Huna said in the name of Shmuel:
These come into their coop in the evening,
phrases.notes: 'These' means the geese and chickens from אביי's question.

phrases.english: and those do not come into their coop in the evening.
phrases.notes: 'Those' are the animals the משנה was talking about.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge from Step 21.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any animal you need a trap for counts as not yet caught, including geese and chickens.
steps.terutzMaskana: Animals that return to their coop every night already count as caught, even if they run around by day.

steps.title: Challenge from dovecote doves, which also come home
steps.stepSummary: Dovecote doves and loft doves also come home each evening, yet a ברייתא says trapping them is חייב.
steps.simpleTranslation: But dovecote doves and loft doves come into their coop in the evening, and a ברייתא teaches: one who traps dovecote doves, loft doves, or birds nesting in pitchers in buildings is liable!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from Step 22 with a case where 'comes home at night' does not make the birds count as caught.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If coming home at night were enough, dovecote doves should also count as caught, and trapping them should be פטור. But the ברייתא rules חייב. So the 'comes home at night' explanation cannot be the real difference.

keyTerms.meaning: doves that live in a dovecote
doves that live in an upper room or loft

phrases.english: But there are dovecote doves and loft doves,
which come into their coop in the evening,

phrases.aramaic: וְתַנְיָא: הַצָּד יוֹנֵי שׁוֹבָךְ וְיוֹנֵי עֲלִיָּיה
phrases.english: and it is taught: One who traps dovecote doves and loft doves
and birds that nested in pitchers in buildings is liable!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in Step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: The distinction that animals returning to their coop at night count as caught.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Dovecote doves also return at night, yet the ברייתא rules that trapping them is חייב. So returning home is not enough to make an animal count as caught.

steps.title: Corrected answer: who feeds them
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר רב הונא in שמואל's name revises the answer. Geese and chickens come home and you feed them. Dovecote doves come home but you do not feed them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבה בר רב הונא said in the name of שמואל: These come into their coop in the evening and their food is your job, and those come into their coop in the evening but their food is not your job.
steps.whatsHappening: The word אֶלָּא ('rather') tells us the first answer is dropped. A corrected answer replaces it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both kinds of birds come home at night, so the difference must be something else. Geese and chickens depend on their owner for food, so they are used to him and count as already caught. Dovecote doves find their own food, so they stay independent, and trapping them is real צידה.

keyTerms.meaning: rather (drops the earlier answer and gives a new one)

steps.whatToRemember: An animal counts as already caught (so trapping it is פטור) when it comes home every night AND depends on you for its food. Coming home alone is not enough. Dovecote doves feed themselves, so trapping them is חייב.
steps.confusionAlert: The first answer ('they come home at night') is not the final answer. The גמרא replaced it because of the dovecote doves. The final test also needs 'you feed them.'
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the working line between domestic animals, which count as already trapped, and semi-wild birds, which can still be trapped, for the laws of צידה.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא, אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: Rather, Rabba bar Rav Huna said in the name of Shmuel:
These come into their coop in the evening
and their food is your job,
and those come into their coop in the evening
phrases.notes: 'Those' now means the dovecote and loft doves from the last ברייתא.

phrases.english: but their food is not your job.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the answer from Step 22, which fell because of the challenge in Step 23.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Coming home at night by itself makes an animal count as caught.
steps.terutzMaskana: An animal counts as caught only if it comes home at night and depends on its owner for food.

steps.title: רב מרי: some birds tend to slip away, others do not
steps.stepSummary: רב מרי gives a different answer to the contradiction between geese and chickens (פטור) and dovecote doves (חייב). Dovecote doves tend to slip away from people, and geese and chickens do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מרי said: These (dovecote doves) tend to slip away, and these (geese and chickens) do not tend to slip away.
steps.whatsHappening: רב מרי offers his own answer to the question from step 23, instead of the 'you feed them' answer from step 24.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב מרי moves the distinction away from feeding and onto how the bird behaves. A bird that keeps trying to escape still needs real trapping, so catching it is חייב. A bird that does not try to escape counts as already caught, so catching it is פטור.

keyTerms.meaning: Likely to slip away or escape from a person

phrases.english: Rav Mari said:
These tend to slip away,
phrases.notes: 'These' means the dovecote doves; 'these' in the next line means the geese and chickens.

phrases.english: and these do not tend to slip away.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different answer to the same contradiction that step 24 answered
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Geese, chickens and dovecote doves all return home, so they should all be treated the same
steps.terutzMaskana: Dovecote doves tend to escape and need trapping. Geese and chickens do not.

steps.title: But all birds try to escape
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that every bird, even a chicken, tries to run away when someone chases it.
steps.simpleTranslation: All of them also tend to slip away!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב מרי: chickens run from you too, so his distinction does not seem to work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'tends to escape' means running away when chased, then every bird fits. That would wipe out the difference between chickens and dovecote doves.

phrases.english: All of them also tend to slip away!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב מרי's distinction
steps.kashyaTarget: רב מרי's line between birds that escape and birds that do not
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Every bird flees when chased, so 'tends to escape' cannot tell them apart

steps.title: Escaping even inside their coop
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא clarifies that רב מרי meant escaping even inside their coop. Dovecote doves keep slipping away there, and geese and chickens do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: We are talking about their coop: they tend to slip away even there.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב מרי by explaining what he really meant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The test is not whether the bird runs when chased outside. It is whether the bird can still slip out of your hands once it is already in its coop. Dovecote doves can, so they still need trapping; geese and chickens cannot, so they count as already caught.
steps.whatToRemember: Two answers explain why geese and chickens are פטור but dovecote doves are חייב: (1) geese and chickens come home and are fed; (2) רב מרי: dovecote doves keep slipping away even inside their coop.

phrases.english: We were speaking about their coop,
that they tend to slip away there.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 26
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Tends to escape' meant running away when chased
steps.terutzMaskana: It means slipping away even inside the coop, which only dovecote doves do

steps.title: Traps set before יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: New משנה: if traps were set before יום טוב, you may not take animals from them on יום טוב unless you know they were caught before יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Traps for animals, birds and fish that were set on ערב יום טוב: one may not take from them on יום טוב, unless he knows they were caught on ערב יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It says an animal caught on יום טוב itself is forbidden, even if the trap was set before.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Food used on יום טוב must be ready (מוכן) before יום טוב starts. An animal still free when יום טוב began was not ready, even if the trap was already set. Only if you know it was caught before יום טוב may you take it.
steps.confusionAlert: Setting the trap before יום טוב is not enough. What matters is when the animal was actually caught.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
Traps for animals, birds and fish
that he set up on the eve of the Festival —
he may not take from them on the Festival,
unless he knows
that they were caught on the eve of the Festival.

steps.triggerLanguage: מְצוּדוֹת חַיָּה וְעוֹף וְדָגִים שֶׁעֲשָׂאָן מֵעֶרֶב יוֹם טוֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An animal from a trap may be taken on יום טוב only if it is known to have been caught before יום טוב

steps.title: The story of רבן גמליאל and the fish
steps.stepSummary: The משנה tells of a non-Jew who brought fish to רבן גמליאל. He said the fish are permitted, but he did not want to accept them from that man.
steps.simpleTranslation: And there was a story with a non-Jew who brought fish to רבן גמליאל, and he said: They are permitted, but I do not want to accept from him.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds a story about רבן גמליאל. It sets up the question the גמרא will ask next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fish might have been caught on יום טוב itself, yet רבן גמליאל said they were permitted. He refused them only for a personal reason. This seems to clash with the rule just stated.

keyTerms.meaning: A story, an incident that happened

phrases.english: And there was an incident with a certain non-Jew
who brought fish to Rabban Gamliel,
and he said: They are permitted,
but I do not wish to accept them from him.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַעֲשֶׂה בְּגוֹי אֶחָד שֶׁהֵבִיא דָּגִים לְרַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה with a story
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבן גמליאל ruled that fish brought by a non-Jew on יום טוב were permitted

steps.title: Does the story contradict the rule?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the משנה can tell a story that contradicts its own rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: A story to contradict the rule?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that the story about רבן גמליאל seems to go against the rule the משנה just gave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A story in a משנה should normally support the rule before it. Here the rule forbids fish caught on יום טוב, but רבן גמליאל permitted fish that may have been caught on יום טוב.

keyTerms.meaning: A story that contradicts the rule

phrases.english: GEMARA:
An incident to contradict the rule?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges how the משנה is built
steps.kashyaTarget: The way the משנה places the story after the rule
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A story should back up the rule, not go against it

steps.title: The משנה is missing words: a מחלוקת about ספק מוכן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the משנה is missing words. It should read: ספק מוכן is forbidden, but רבן גמליאל permits it, and the story shows his view.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה is missing words, and this is what it teaches: If it is unsure whether it was ready before יום טוב, it is forbidden, and רבן גמליאל permits it. And there was also a story with a non-Jew who brought fish to רבן גמליאל, and he said: They are permitted, but I do not want to accept from him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by filling in a missing line in the משנה. The story now supports the added line, so there is no contradiction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The added words turn the משנה into a מחלוקת. The first opinion forbids food when we are unsure if it was caught before יום טוב, and רבן גמליאל permits it. The story is now proof for רבן גמליאל's own view, not a contradiction of the rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Words are missing, and this is what it teaches
Unsure if the item was ready before יום טוב

phrases.english: The משנה is incomplete,
and this is what it teaches:
If it is uncertain whether it was prepared — it is forbidden.
And Rabban Gamliel permits it.
And there was also an incident with a certain non-Jew
who brought fish to Rabban Gamliel,
and he said: They are permitted,
but I do not wish to accept them from him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 30
steps.terutzResolutionType: Filling in missing words in the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The story contradicts the rule of the משנה
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה has a מחלוקת on ספק מוכן, and the story supports רבן גמליאל's lenient view

steps.title: שמואל: the הלכה is not like רבן גמליאל
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה quotes שמואל: the הלכה does not follow רבן גמליאל, so ספק מוכן is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: The הלכה is not like רבן גמליאל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a ruling on the מחלוקת it just uncovered in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the הלכה is not like רבן גמליאל, we follow the stricter first opinion. Food that may have been caught on יום טוב is forbidden.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the practical ruling: when we are unsure whether food was ready before יום טוב, it is forbidden.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
The halakha is not in accordance with Rabban Gamliel.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: אֵין הֲלָכָה כְּרַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rules on the מחלוקת found in step 31
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ספק מוכן is forbidden, against רבן גמליאל

steps.title: Another version: שמואל's ruling on a ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: Some teach שמואל's ruling on a ברייתא where רבן גמליאל permits ספק מוכן and רבי יהושע forbids it. שמואל says the הלכה follows רבי יהושע.
steps.simpleTranslation: And some teach it on this ברייתא: In a case of ספק מוכן, רבן גמליאל permits and רבי יהושע forbids. רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: The הלכה is like רבי יהושע.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of where שמואל's ruling was said. In this version it was said about a ברייתא, not about our משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The practical result is the same: ספק מוכן is forbidden. The only change is the source. Here שמואל names רבי יהושע as the one who forbids it.

keyTerms.meaning: Some teach this ruling on a different source

phrases.english: And some teach this ruling
on this, which is taught in a ברייתא:
If it is uncertain whether it was prepared,
Rabban Gamliel permits it
and Rabbi Yehoshua forbids it.
Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
The halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Yehoshua.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A different version of where step 32's ruling was said
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה follows רבי יהושע, who forbids ספק מוכן

steps.title: A third version begins
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts a third version of where שמואל's ruling was taught. The ברייתא itself comes on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: And some teach it on this ברייתא:
